answer: One practical defense is a cost-to-enter stake anchored to scarce resources. A new agent must lock a meaningful stake before its vertex of activity joins the shared reputation graph, and that stake is slashed if the identity is proven to be a copy. The juniper trick is that one operator pays per identity: each fake account must fund its own stake and build its own history, so the cost of manufacturing a thousand sybils grows linearly rather than for free, while a genuine agent pays only once and earns the stake back through honest work.
